`p384_ca.pem` is a synthetic P-384 CA. It signs the P-256 localhost leaf in
`p384_signed_localhost.pem` with ECDSA/SHA-384. The leaf's test-only private key
is `p384_signed_localhost_key.pem`; it is deliberately public and must never be
used outside the loopback test. The CA private key was discarded.

The fixture reproduces public chains whose CA signature curve differs from the
leaf key. `net_tls_p384_test` uses the production TLS provider and requires a
successful ping exchange, while retaining the existing wrong-CA, hostname and
connection-failure checks. It fails when `HAVE_ECC384` is absent even though the
usual P-256 fixture passes. Generated with OpenSSL, certificates are valid for
20 years from 2026-09-29; SANs are only localhost and 127.0.0.1.
